Antimicrobial use as a rate, in one call

Source: R/org.R
op_antibiotic_use.Rd

Combines op_spending_ab(), op_org_details() and op_rate(): downloads prescribing for the requested antimicrobials, downloads the denominator at the same organisation level, and returns items per 1,000 registered patients (or another denominator).

Usage

op_antibiotic_use(
  x,
  org_type = "national",
  org = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  denominator = "total_list_size",
  per = 1000,
  scope = c("systemic", "all"),
  use_amr = TRUE,
  progress = interactive()
)

Arguments

x

Antimicrobial names, AMR codes, ATC codes/prefixes or group names (see ab_to_bnf()).

org_type

Organisation level: "national" (all of England, default), "sicbl" (Sub-ICB Location, formerly CCG), "icb", "pcn", "practice" or "regional_team".

org

Optional organisation code(s) (for example a Sub-ICB code such as "15N" or a practice code such as "H81068"). For "practice", a Sub-ICB code returns all its practices. If NULL, all organisations of that type are returned.

date

Optional month(s) as "YYYY-MM", "YYYY-MM-DD" or Date. Required for org_type = "practice" when org is NULL (the API refuses to return every practice for every month). Several dates trigger one request per date.

denominator

Denominator key from op_org_details(); default "total_list_size". "star_pu.oral_antibacterial_items" gives STAR-PU weighted rates.

per

Scaling factor (default 1000).

scope

"systemic" (default) keeps BNF chapter 5 (infections: oral and injectable products). "all" also returns topical, eye, ear, skin and vaginal chemicals from chapters 7, 11, 12 and 13, which are prescribed for different purposes and should not be pooled with systemic use by accident.

use_amr

Use AMR::as.ab() for inputs the bundled table cannot resolve (default TRUE; ignored if AMR is not installed).

progress

Show a progress bar when several requests are needed (default: only in interactive sessions).

Value

A data frame as from op_spending_ab() plus the denominator column and rate.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
use <- op_antibiotic_use(c("amoxicillin", "nitrofurantoin"), org_type = "sicbl", org = "15N")
op_plot_trend(use, y = "rate")
} # }
